newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign investors' purchases of Danish bonds soar.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors' purchases of Danish bonds soar.

text.p: Foreign investors' purchases of Danish bonds rose in May to 10.7 billion crowns, from 4.2 billion in April, while share purchases dropped to 0.1 billion crowns from 0.3 billion, the central bank said.

The bank's monthly report showed that foreign purchases of government bonds rose to 9.0 billion crowns from 3.1 billion, while mortgage-backed bonds showed a far more modest rise, to 1.7 billion crowns in May from 1.1 the month before.
Over the 12 months to end-May 1997, however, mortgage-backed bonds dominated, with foreign purchases of 21.1 billion crowns as against government paper of 13.1 billion.
In the same period the year before, mortgage-backed paper sold for 10.1 billion and state bonds for 18.4 billion crowns.

Annualised share sales to foreign buyers totalled 12.0 billion crowns to end-May 1997, up from 6.8 billion in the 12 months to end-May 1996, the bank said. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
